notes: Lead: Dan Morales (CTO). Primary goal: low-latency assistant for content editors across NA/EU.
Initial complaint: 'EU editors see slow response times on short chat queries (~1.5s) compared to demo'
Traffic profile: unpredictable bursts e.g., product releases -> concurrent active users ~50-200, typical requests small (40-150 tokens), occasional long-summary jobs (600-1k tokens)
They are self-serve signups, want to avoid long procurement but need simple written assurances for retention and SSO.
Perf takeaways from initial tests: EU region median latency higher; suspect routing + cold starts + model selection.
technical_observations: Observed request samples show heavy system prompt (600+ tokens) appended for each chat -> increases per-call latency and cost
They used a 30s http timeout; front-end aborts earlier leading to retries and perceived slowness
No prefix caching in client; repeated intro text sent every call
Model used in POC: redwood/gpt-3.5-like-large (default) - consider smaller variant for majority short chats
recommended_actions: Advise region: route NA -> us-east-1 or us-west-2, EU -> eu-west-1; run short A/B test to confirm median latency
Timeouts: set client-side non-streaming timeout 10s for short chat, 30s for long generation; streaming keepalive 60s
Prompt guidance: move static system context to server-side prefix caching; compress template to <200 tokens where possible
Model tuning: use smaller low-latency model for short interactions, fall back to large for long summarization (auto-fallback policy)
Batching: enable small batching (window 5-10ms) for bursts to improve throughput without adding visible latency
Monitoring: add per-route p50/p95/p99 in Console + token cost dashboard; create alert if p95 > 800ms in region
